title: Why State Management Matters 🧠
description: Learn what state is and why managing it with plain services often leads to bugs.

slides.title: What Is State? 🗂️
slides.content:
# State = Data that changes over time

Every interactive application has **state**:
* The current user (logged in or not).
* Items in a shopping cart.
* An array of search results.
* UI flags (sidebar open/closed, loading spinner visible).

When state changes, the UI must update. In Angular, we often keep state in services and use Observables to broadcast changes.

slides.title: The Problem with Mutable Shared State 🐛
slides.content:
When multiple components directly mutate a plain object stored in a service, tracking **who changed what and when** becomes impossible.

* Bugs arise: one component overwrites another’s data.
* Change detection may not run (if object reference doesn’t change).
* It’s hard to debug or replay state transitions.

We need a **single source of truth** that components can **observe** but not directly mutate.

quizData.question: What is a major risk of letting any component directly mutate a shared object in a service?

options.text: It’s impossible to track who changed the data, leading to unpredictable UI.
The template can no longer display the data.

quizData.explanation: Without controlled mutations, state becomes unpredictable and debugging is a nightmare.

slides.title: The RxJS Solution: Observables as State 📡
slides.content:
Instead of exposing raw data, expose an **Observable stream** of state updates. Components subscribe and react automatically.

* Use a **Subject** (like BehaviorSubject) to hold the current state and emit new values.
* The service is the **single source of truth**: only the service can change the state.
* Components dispatch **actions** (method calls) to the service, which updates the state and notifies subscribers.

This is the **store pattern** – you don’t need a library like NgRx to do it.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep the Subject Private

Never expose the Subject directly. Only expose the Observable (`asObservable()`). This prevents external code from calling `.next()` and bypassing your business logic.

quizData.question: It's safe to expose a Subject directly from a service so components can emit new values.
quizData.explanation: Exposing the Subject lets anyone call .next(), undermining control over state changes.
